clue.text: In a way, Conservative Party's conclusion is irregular

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for a way, which wraps round it
the conclusion of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: a path is a way to walk along
C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative
the final letter of party

explanation.surface: A political party whose final policy statement turns out to be inconsistent and erratic.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation for Conservative sits inside the word for a way, and the last letter of Party follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uneven in quality, good in places and poor in others, is described as patchy.

clue.text: Job description invariably mentions this virtue

definitions.text: Job description invariably mentions this virtue

blocks.note: surface reading: an employer's written outline of the duties of a post

blocks.clueFragment: Job description invariably mentions this virtue
blocks.note: setter's reading: Job is the biblical figure, and any account of him praises his long-suffering endurance

explanation.surface: Every job advert seems to list the same desirable personal quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' at the start of the clue hides its capital: it is the Old Testament sufferer, proverbial for the patience of Job.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical Job endured every misfortune without cursing God, so the virtue always linked with his name is calm endurance.

clue.text: Proposition from opponents of US about mineral

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word is wrapped round the second

blocks.note: seen from our side, the opposition is them as against us
ore is a mineral that is mined

explanation.surface: A political proposal from America's enemies concerning some mineral resource.
explanation.walkthrough: US is not America here but the pronoun us, whose opposite number is them.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a theorem is a proposition, a statement put forward to be proved.

clue.text: Organ conductor found in centre of Poplar, say

blocks.note: the heart is a bodily organ
Sir Henry Wood, the conductor who founded the Proms concerts

explanation.surface: An organist and conductor turn up in the middle of Poplar, a district of east London.
explanation.walkthrough: Poplar looks like the London district, but 'say' marks it as an example of a tree, whose dense middle timber is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartwood is the hard, dead inner wood at the core of a tree trunk such as a poplar.

clue.text: Undercoat ornamental trim

blocks.note: first meaning, read cryptically: a coat of fur lying beneath, split as two words
second meaning: a flounce or ruffle on a dress

explanation.surface: A dressmaker's note: an undercoat finished with decorative edging.
explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is a pun: split the answer into two words and it describes a coat lying underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A furbelow is a flounce or ruffle on a skirt or petticoat, a showy decorative edging on a garment.

clue.text: Poor German's at his workplace, according to Cockney

indicators.note: this is how a Londoner from the East End would pronounce the words, so we go by their sound

blocks.note: a German is a Hun in old slang and a workplace a factory; a Cockney drops the h from Hun and his

explanation.surface: A German worker's job is poorly regarded, as described by a Londoner.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class East London accent, famous for dropping initial h sounds; Hun is a dated slang term for a German.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor work is substandard, failing to meet the required level, which is what unsatisfactory means.

clue.text: Obscure plot I am following

blocks.note: a plot in a garden is a flower bed
I am contracts to I'm

explanation.surface: A conspirator admits to being behind some murky scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: Plot is a garden plot, not a scheme, and 'following' puts I'm after it.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to obscure something is to make it dim or hard to see, which is to bedim it.

clue.text: Part of table allowed in short publication

blocks.note: a leaf is a hinged or removable section of a table top
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A short pamphlet says what may be put on a table.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaflet is a printed sheet or small folded pamphlet, a brief item handed out to readers.

clue.text: Secure score that's typical of season

blocks.note: to secure a prize is to win it
in rugby a try is a score made by grounding the ball

explanation.surface: A sports team clinches a seasonal result with a characteristic goal.
explanation.walkthrough: The season is a time of year rather than a sporting season; a try is the main way of scoring in rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintry describes weather or scenes characteristic of the coldest time of the year.

clue.text: Some such leaders impress in one term, possibly

definitions.note: the clue's own leaders, read as a class of heads of government

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters before it may be reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some national leaders make a strong impression within a single period in office.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is almost a description of the answer: a few heads of government do make their mark in one term.
explanation.definitionFit: Prime ministers are heads of government in parliamentary systems, the kind of leaders who serve terms of office.

clue.text: Reference work a user ordered, therefore, taken round

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new sequence, so the letters are rearranged
taken round means carried around something, so one word goes outside the other

blocks.note: thus means therefore
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A reader orders a reference book, which is consequently delivered to them.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a reference book listing words grouped by meaning, with their synonyms.

clue.text: Lured northward in retreat

indicators.note: a retreating army goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: north is abbreviated to N, and ward is kept as written

explanation.surface: Someone is enticed to head north as a retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northward' splits into north, abbreviated, and ward; the whole thing then goes backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To be drawn somewhere is to be attracted or pulled there, the same as being lured.

clue.text: One slip followed by another?

blocks.note: surface reading: a run of mistakes, one blunder after another
setter's reading: a printing mistake in a book is followed by a separate paper slip listing the correction

explanation.walkthrough: Slip means first a mistake and then a loose sheet of paper inserted into a book.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error in printing or writing, often listed on a correction slip pasted into the book.

clue.text: He was in the Middle East in order to get a lawyer

definitions.text: He was in the Middle East in order

blocks.clueFragment: He was in the Middle East in order
blocks.note: first meaning: a member of the Knights ..., the crusading military order based in Jerusalem
second meaning: a barrister or law student with chambers in the Temple, an Inn of Court in London

explanation.surface: A man went to the Middle East to find himself a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In order' sounds like 'so as to', but it means belonging to a religious order. The Inner and Middle Temple are two of the London Inns of Court where barristers train.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a crusading knight of a medieval military order and a lawyer based at London's Temple.

clue.text: Group formed by bishop in Italian city

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation inside the city name, which surrounds it

blocks.note: Como is a city on Lake Como in northern Italy
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A church group set up by a bishop based in an Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: A combo is a small band of musicians, especially in jazz, so a musical group.

clue.text: It can spread disease, hence doctors must have capital

blocks.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor; MOs are doctors
Quito is the capital of Ecuador

explanation.surface: An epidemic is spreading, so the capital city needs more doctors.
explanation.definitionFit: The mosquito is an insect whose bite transmits illnesses such as malaria and dengue.

clue.text: Maiden not harmed if abandoned by one

indicators.note: if the answer were abandoned by one it would read as the wordplay word, so one belongs inside that word

blocks.note: unmarred means undamaged, not harmed
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A girl comes out unscathed, provided a single person leaves her alone.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer, abandoned by one, would read 'not harmed'; so one must be put back inside that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Maiden used as an adjective describes a woman who has never had a husband, as in maiden name.

clue.text: Cast off in storm

blocks.note: surface reading: a boat untied from its moorings during bad weather
setter's reading: cargo thrown overboard to lighten a ship in danger at sea

explanation.walkthrough: Cast off looks like a sailor releasing a rope; it is goods thrown off the ship to save it.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw goods overboard from a ship, typically in an emergency such as heavy weather.

clue.text: Reading a novel in one sort of tree.

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters are made into something new

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sits reading a novel up in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel looks like the book being read, but as an adjective it means new and changes the letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardenias are evergreen shrubs and small trees with fragrant white flowers, so one kind of tree.

clue.text: Nearly all for money's here by time specified

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the ready is slang for cash; ready money is money here to hand

explanation.surface: Almost everything for the funding has arrived by the deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: The ready is old British slang for cash in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means before now or before some stated moment, as in the work was finished by then.

clue.text: ...or another, he includes extra page

definitions.note: continues the previous clue: another sort of tree

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so the second piece goes inside the first

blocks.note: he refers to a male
P is the abbreviation for page, the extra one added

explanation.surface: A writer adds one more page to his book.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots tie this clue to 18 across, whose definition was one sort of tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple is a tree, just as the gardenia of the previous clue is one sort of tree.

clue.text: Posture, for him, liable to change

definitions.text: Posture, for him, liable to change

indicators.note: something liable to change will not stay as it is, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A character whose stance is always shifting.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: the Greek sea god could change his shape at will.
explanation.definitionFit: Proteus was the old man of the sea in Greek myth, a god who escaped capture by constantly changing form.

clue.text: Vehicle looked over by driver

blocks.note: surface reading: a car inspected by its driver before setting off
setter's reading: a horse-drawn cab whose driver sits on a raised seat behind, looking over its roof

explanation.walkthrough: Looked over means literally gazed across the top of, as the coachman did from his perch at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A hansom is a two-wheeled horse-drawn cab, with the driver seated high up behind the passengers.

clue.text: A supporter's seen outside Oval, by the way

indicators.note: seen outside means placed on the outside, so the supporter's letters go round the round shape

blocks.note: taken as written
a prop is a supporter; with the 's attached
an oval is O-shaped

explanation.surface: A fan is spotted outside the Oval, mentioned in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground, but here it is just the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos, used as an aside, introduces a related point in the way that by the way does.

clue.text: Echo in prison cell

blocks.note: first meaning: in bridge, playing a high card then a low one as a signal to partner, also called an echo
second meaning: old criminal slang for a cell in jail

explanation.surface: A voice rings back from inside a jail cell.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are specialist: one comes from bridge signalling, the other from underworld slang.
explanation.definitionFit: In card play the high-low signal is called both an echo and a peter, and criminals once called a prison cell a peter.

clue.text: Discharge those people who appear

blocks.note: first meaning: to ... is to expel or send away
second meaning: the number attending an event

explanation.surface: Dismissing the crowd that has gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense is two words, turn out; the noun is written as one.
explanation.definitionFit: Turn out means to eject someone, and a turnout is the body of people attending an event or election.

clue.text: Jump the signal to proceed

blocks.note: first meaning: a sudden jerk of surprise
second meaning: the go-ahead for a race to begin

explanation.surface: A runner leaves early before the official go-ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests jumping the gun, a false start; the two meanings are taken separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A start is a sudden jump of alarm, and also the beginning signal given to runners in a race.

clue.text: Property developed to make a man wealthy etc

definitions.text: Property developed to make a man wealthy etc

blocks.clueFragment: Property developed to make a man wealthy
blocks.note: surface reading: real estate built up to make an investor rich

blocks.clueFragment: Property developed to make a man wealthy etc
blocks.note: setter's reading: the habit of going to bed and rising in good time, as in the proverb about healthy, wealthy and wise

explanation.walkthrough: Property is a quality, not land; the etc points to the proverb early to bed and early to rise makes a man healthy, wealthy and wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Earliness is the quality of being in good time, the habit the old proverb says brings health and riches.

clue.text: Corporation official says more when drunk

indicators.note: a drunk person's words come out jumbled, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A town hall dignitary gets talkative after a few drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: A corporation here is a town council, not a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayoress is a female mayor or the mayor's wife acting as civic hostess, an office of a town council.

clue.text: Remarkable child most likely to succeed

blocks.note: odd means strange, remarkable
a son is a child

explanation.surface: An unusual youngster who is tipped for great things.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, a horse at odds-on is the favourite, judged the likeliest to win.
